# Notion — Style Reference

> Diluted ink on a white notebook page, one cobalt button. Tightly tracked Inter-cut grotesk, a white sheet with a faint warm wash, hairlines at 10% black, and a single cobalt button that only means go.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Notion speaks an alpha-ink document language. Every text tone is pure black thinned by opacity rather than a hand-mixed gray: #000000f2 for display, #000000e5 for body, #0000008a for captions. The page is a #ffffff sheet with #f9f9f8 Linen Wash panels laid on top of it. The chromatic budget is one hue. Lapis Signal #0075de fills the primary button, and its #e6f3fe tint with #005bab ink builds the secondary. Every other saturated color lives inside illustrations, product mockups and testimonial duotones as decoration. Typography is one customized Inter at weights 400 to 700. Display sizes are tracked hard (-4.6px at 96px, about -0.048em) and climb on a Perfect Fourth from 42px to 96px, so weight and tracking carry hierarchy, not color. Shapes are soft: 8px buttons, 12px cards and a single 9999px highlight pill that punctuates the headline. Elevation is either a 10% black hairline or a layered shadow that tops out at 0.04 alpha. The result reads as a working document rather than a marketing billboard.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Page ground, nav bar, footer, use-case tiles and the white mock cards inside panels (18 uses) — the sheet every alpha-ink tone is mixed against. |
| Linen Wash | `#f9f9f8` | `--color-linen-wash` | Feature panels under "AI where your team works" and the agent showcase (6 uses) — a warm 1% shift that separates zones without a border or shadow. |
| Ink | `#000000` | `--color-ink` | 22px card titles, 16px tile titles and the circular arrow chips (13 text plus 3 fill uses) — full-strength black reserved for clickable headings and the inverted chip. |
| Jet Display | `#000000f2` | `--color-jet-display` | The 96px hero headline, 54px section headings and the logo mark — 95% black that softens the darkest pixels at display sizes. |
| Carbon Body | `#000000e5` | `--color-carbon-body` | Body copy, nav links, hero subhead and footer text (32 uses, the workhorse) — 90% black keeps long reading quieter than pure ink. |
| Charcoal Mark | `#000000bf` | `--color-charcoal-mark` | Customer logos in the trust strip, rendered as masks (17 uses) — 75% black flattens every brand into one tone so no partner outshouts the page. |
| Pebble Stat | `#615d59` | `--color-pebble-stat` | Proof-point lines such as "100M users in over 50 countries" (15 uses) — the only warm opaque gray, deliberately tied to the warmth of Linen Wash. |
| Graphite Caption | `#0000008a` | `--color-graphite-caption` | Eyebrows, the "See what Notion can do" label and the logo-strip caption (9 uses) — 54% black that recedes behind every heading. |
| Ash Border | `#0000001a` | `--color-ash-border` | 1px edges on use-case tiles and the divider above the logo strip (7 uses) — a hairline that replaces shadow as the default edge. |
| Lapis Signal | `#0075de` | `--color-lapis-signal` | "Get Notion free" fills in the nav and hero, plus the in-mockup "New" button — the only saturated system fill. Do not use it for headings, icons or section backgrounds. |
| Lapis Ink | `#005bab` | `--color-lapis-ink` | Text of the "Request a demo" secondary button — a darker step of the same hue that keeps the secondary in the blue family without competing as a fill. |
| Lapis Mist | `#e6f3fe` | `--color-lapis-mist` | Fill of the secondary "Request a demo" button — a 10% tint that reads as the primary's shadow-self. Do not use it as a section background. |
| Apricot Highlight | `#ffdec4` | `--color-apricot-highlight` | The pill behind the word "Create" in the hero headline (1 use) — a highlighter stroke drawn across a document. Keep it to one word per page. |

## Tokens — Typography

### NotionInter — The single grotesk that does display, UI and body work · `--font-notioninter`

- **Substitute:** Inter at matching weights (400 body, 500 UI, 600 and 700 display); Inter Display at 600 for the 96px headline; Geist at 500 for UI text. NotionInter renders true to its nominal weight, so no weight correction is needed.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 12px, 14px, 16px, 20px, 22px, 42px, 54px, 72px, 96px
- **Line height:** 1.04 (54px, 96px), 1.14 (42px), 1.21 (72px), 1.27 (22px), 1.33 (12px), 1.4 (20px), 1.43 (14px), 1.5 (16px)
- **Letter spacing:** 0.125px at 12px; 0px at 14px and 16px; -0.125px at 20px; -0.25px at 22px; -1.5px at 42px; -1.875px at 54px; -2px at 72px; -4.6px at 96px
- **OpenType features:** `lnum`, `locl 0`
- **Role:** Weight 500 at 14px is the most-used setting (47 elements), so the UI voice is slightly firmer than the 400 most marketing sites default to. That is the product's own interface leaking onto the page. Display tracking tightens from -0.031em at 42px to -0.048em at 96px, far beyond the -0.02em convention, so headlines lock into dense black slabs. The top of the scale steps 42, 54, 72, 96, roughly a Perfect Fourth (1.333). The bottom steps 12, 14, 16, roughly 1.14, tighter than a Minor Third, which compresses body sizes and dramatizes the jump to display.

### Lyon Text — An editorial serif reserved for quoted voices · `--font-lyon-text`

- **Substitute:** Source Serif 4 at 400; Newsreader Text at 450; Literata at 400. Lyon draws sturdier than most book serifs, so take the heavier option when choosing between Newsreader cuts.
- **Weights:** 400
- **Sizes:** 16px, 18px
- **Line height:** 1.5 (16px), 1.56 (18px)
- **Letter spacing:** 0px at 16px and 18px
- **OpenType features:** `liga`, `lnum`, `locl 0`
- **Role:** Four elements use Lyon Text, all at weight 400 and at body sizes only. It is the voice of a quoted person rather than the voice of the product. Pairing a book serif with a grotesk is a conventional editorial move, but rationing it this hard means the serif signals "someone else is speaking" every time it appears.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | NotionInter | 500 | 12px | 1.33 | 0.125px | `--text-small` |
| caption | NotionInter | 400 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | NotionInter | 500 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | NotionInter | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | NotionInter | 400 | 20px | 1.4 | -0.125px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | NotionInter | 600 | 20px | 1.4 | -0.125px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | NotionInter | 700 | 22px | 1.27 | -0.25px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | NotionInter | 700 | 42px | 1.14 | -1.5px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | NotionInter | 700 | 54px | 1.04 | -1.875px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | NotionInter | 600 | 96px | 1.04 | -4.6px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every text tone as black at an alpha — #000000f2 for display, #000000e5 for body, #0000008a for captions — so type always takes its temperature from the paper beneath it.
- Spend #0075de only on the primary action, at most one filled button per viewport cluster — a single blue pixel budget turns the button into the page's only signal.
- Track display type hard: -4.6px at 96px, -1.875px at 54px, -1.5px at 42px — the tight fit turns headlines into dense ink blocks instead of airy captions.
- Use 8px radius on every button and 12px on every card — two soft steps keep the vocabulary close to the product's own UI chrome.
- Edge flat tiles with 1px solid #0000001a before reaching for a shadow — hairlines carry structure at 10% black without lifting anything off the page.
- Keep every shadow layer at or below 0.04 alpha, stacked across 4 to 6 stops as in shadow-sm and shadow-lg — elevation should be felt, not seen.
- Pair the #0075de primary with the #e6f3fe and #005bab secondary at an identical 38px height and 6px 15px padding — that matched pair is non-negotiable, because it makes two actions read as one decision.

### Don't

- Don't color a headline #0075de for emphasis — hierarchy here is ink density and tracking, black thinned by alpha, so a blue heading reads as a link and spends the only accent.
- Don't promote the illustration hues (#f64932, #ffb110, #1aae39 — decorative) to buttons, badges or section fills — they exist inside drawings and photos, and loosening them dissolves the one-blue budget.
- Don't leave display letter spacing at 0px on 96px type — the letters drift 4.6px apart and the headline loses its slab-like density.
- Don't round buttons to 9999px — the pill shape belongs to the 72px #ffdec4 highlight alone, and pill buttons would turn annotation into chrome.
- Don't replace the 0.04-alpha layered shadows with a conventional single drop at 0.15 or 0.2 alpha — that is four to five times the ceiling and makes paper cards look like plastic.
- Don't push weights past 700 or drop display below 600 at 96px — the system's contrast lives between 400 body and 600/700 headings, and 800 or 900 turns a document into a poster.
- Don't make the 64px nav sticky with a backdrop blur — the bar never floats on this page, and pinning it adds app chrome to what is meant to scroll like a document.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- panel surface: #f9f9f8 (Linen Wash)
- display text: #000000f2 (Jet Display)
- body text: #000000e5 (Carbon Body)
- caption text: #0000008a (Graphite Caption)
- hairline: #0000001a (Ash Border)
- highlight: #ffdec4 (Apricot Highlight)
- primary action: #0075de (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts inside product mockups may use solid decorative fills such as #1aae39 and #f64932 as illustration, but any system-level data visualization stays neutral in #000000e5 and #0000008a, with #0075de at a 10% tint (#e6f3fe) for one highlighted series, so the button remains the loudest blue on the page.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: an anchor with background #0075de, text #ffffff, a 1px solid transparent border, border-radius 8px, padding 6px 15px and a total height of 38px. Set it in NotionInter (fallback Inter) at 16px, weight 500, line-height 24px, letter-spacing 0px, with no shadow. Beside it, 12px to the right, place the secondary: background #e6f3fe, text #005bab, with the same border, 8px radius, 6px 15px padding, 38px height and 16px weight 500 type.

2. Build a hero section on #ffffff with a 1252px max-width, centered. Add an h1 in NotionInter at 96px, weight 600, line-height 100px, letter-spacing -4.6px, color #000000f2, across two lines. Wrap one word in an inline span with background #ffdec4, border-radius 9999px, padding 8px 28px, font-size 72px, weight 500 and letter-spacing -2px. Below it, set a 20px weight 400 subhead in #000000e5 with -0.125px tracking and line-height 28px, 16px under the headline. Then add the primary and secondary buttons, 24px below the subhead. Then place a 1250px product screenshot with 12px top-corner radius and the six-layer shadow-lg, 64px below the buttons.

3. Build a feature panel: background #f9f9f8, no border, border-radius 12px, padding 24px. Add a 14px weight 400 eyebrow in #0000008a, then 4px below it a 22px weight 700 title in #000000 with letter-spacing -0.25px and line-height 28px. Place a 24px circle on the right edge of the title row, filled #000000 with border-radius 50% and a white arrow. Below, 24px down, nest a #ffffff card with 12px top-corner radius and shadow-sm containing a product screenshot.

4. Build a use-case tile row: five tiles in a grid with 8px gaps beneath a 14px weight 400 #0000008a label. Each tile has background #ffffff, border 1px solid #0000001a, border-radius 12px, padding 24px and height 160px, with a 32px illustrated icon at the top and, 24px below it, a 16px weight 700 title in #000000 with line-height 24px ending in "→". No shadow.

5. Build a navigation bar 64px tall on #ffffff with position relative, no border and no shadow. Put a 33px black logo on the left. In the center, place text links in NotionInter 16px weight 400, color #000000e5, padding 5px 10px, border-radius 4px, with a hover background of #0000001a. On the right, put "Log in" in the same style followed by a primary button with background #0075de, 8px radius, 4px 14px padding and 36px height.

**Role:** Full product screenshot as proof

The product is the hero image. A 1250 × 781px screenshot of a Notion workspace with sidebar, board view and status columns, framed with 12px top-corner radius on a #ffffff surface and lifted by the six-layer shadow-lg. Hand-drawn ink characters peek over its edges. The heaviest shadow on the page goes to the product itself, and the 0.04 alpha ceiling keeps even that lift lighter than a conventional device-mockup drop shadow.

### Feature Panel — Linen Wash (Main Content Card)
**Role:** Hosts one capability with screenshot

A tinted tray, not a box. Background #f9f9f8, no border, 12px radius and 24px padding, carrying a 14px #0000008a eyebrow, a NotionInter 22px weight 700 title in #000000 with -0.25px tracking, and a circular arrow chip at the right. A white mock card with shadow-sm and 12px top corners sits inside it. Panels pair two-up, then run full width. Tonal layering, not outline, defines the panel.

### Arrow Chip — Ink (Inverted)
**Role:** Affordance that a panel opens

The sole inverted surface. A 24px circle (estimated) filled #000000 with a white arrow glyph and 50% radius, aligned to the panel title's right edge. Where a conventional site would add a "Learn more" text link, this uses a solid black dot. Black works here because color is reserved for the conversion button, which keeps the panel's own call to action monochrome.

### Use-Case Tile — Hairline
**Role:** Quick-link grid to agent templates

Paper card with a pen line. Background #ffffff, 1px solid #0000001a border, 12px radius, 24px padding and 160px height, with a 32px illustrated icon on top and a NotionInter 16px weight 700 title in #000000 ending in an arrow. Five tiles sit in a row with 8px gaps under a 14px #0000008a label. The icon colors (#1aae39, #1313ba and others) are decorative, not system tokens. The hairline-over-shadow choice keeps a dense row from stacking into visual noise.

### Logo Strip — Monotone
**Role:** Social proof without color noise

A flattened roll call. A 14px weight 400 caption in #0000008a sits centered above a full-width 1px #0000001a divider, followed by two rows of nine customer marks masked to #000000bf, separated by small dots. Converting every brand to one 75% black tone is deliberately anti-convention: OpenAI, Toyota and Figma become equal-weight words, and the strip stays subordinate to the headline above it.

### Testimonial Video Card — Duotone
**Role:** Customer story with face

The loudest color on the page, and decorative only. Each card is a portrait washed in a single duotone (red #f64932, blue #097fe8, amber #ffb110 — decorative, not system tokens) with the customer's logo in white at the top left. Corners are 12px, there is no border and no shadow, and three cards sit side by side under a 54px weight 700 heading. Saturation is quarantined inside photography, so it never contaminates the interface palette.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every text tone as black at an alpha — #000000f2 for display, #000000e5 for body, #0000008a for captions — so type always takes its temperature from the paper beneath it.
- Spend #0075de only on the primary action, at most one filled button per viewport cluster — a single blue pixel budget turns the button into the page's only signal.
- Track display type hard: -4.6px at 96px, -1.875px at 54px, -1.5px at 42px — the tight fit turns headlines into dense ink blocks instead of airy captions.
- Use 8px radius on every button and 12px on every card — two soft steps keep the vocabulary close to the product's own UI chrome.
- Edge flat tiles with 1px solid #0000001a before reaching for a shadow — hairlines carry structure at 10% black without lifting anything off the page.
- Keep every shadow layer at or below 0.04 alpha, stacked across 4 to 6 stops as in shadow-sm and shadow-lg — elevation should be felt, not seen.
- Pair the #0075de primary with the #e6f3fe and #005bab secondary at an identical 38px height and 6px 15px padding — that matched pair is non-negotiable, because it makes two actions read as one decision.

### Don't

- Don't color a headline #0075de for emphasis — hierarchy here is ink density and tracking, black thinned by alpha, so a blue heading reads as a link and spends the only accent.
- Don't promote the illustration hues (#f64932, #ffb110, #1aae39 — decorative) to buttons, badges or section fills — they exist inside drawings and photos, and loosening them dissolves the one-blue budget.
- Don't leave display letter spacing at 0px on 96px type — the letters drift 4.6px apart and the headline loses its slab-like density.
- Don't round buttons to 9999px — the pill shape belongs to the 72px #ffdec4 highlight alone, and pill buttons would turn annotation into chrome.
- Don't replace the 0.04-alpha layered shadows with a conventional single drop at 0.15 or 0.2 alpha — that is four to five times the ceiling and makes paper cards look like plastic.
- Don't push weights past 700 or drop display below 600 at 96px — the system's contrast lives between 400 body and 600/700 headings, and 800 or 900 turns a document into a poster.
- Don't make the 64px nav sticky with a backdrop blur — the bar never floats on this page, and pinning it adds app chrome to what is meant to scroll like a document.

## Imagery

Imagery is the product itself plus hand-drawn ink illustration. Real Notion screenshots dominate: the hero workspace, the Meetings database, the H2 Deal Flow dashboard and the Coding Agent chat. They are framed with 12px top corners on #ffffff, either seated inside #f9f9f8 panels or floating on shadow-lg. Black-line doodle characters with crosshatched clothing and tiny color-dot props peek over the frame edges, which is a sketchbook gesture rather than conventional 3D render art. Icons are small illustrated stickers in flat saturated fills (decorative, not system tokens). Testimonials switch to duotone portrait video in red, blue and amber. There are no gradients, glows or orbs anywhere in the system. The narrative is a working notebook: the actual tool, annotated by hand.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1252px column centered on a 1920px canvas, with 1184px for the logo strip. Sections are separated by about 96px, stretching to 141px before testimonials. The hero is fully centered: a two-line 96px headline with the apricot pill inline, a 20px subhead, and two 38px buttons 12px apart. A 1250px product screenshot follows. The logo strip runs two rows of nine. Below it, sections switch to left alignment: a 54px heading, then two 12px-radius Linen panels side by side, then one full-width panel, then a five-column hairline tile row and a three-column testimonial row. There is no pricing grid on the home page. The nav is 64px, white and non-sticky, with the logo left, links center and Log in plus the CTA right. The footer is white with 80px top and 24px bottom padding. At 375px, use the 42px heading size as display and 64px section gaps, and stack all grids to one column. Overall density is comfortable.

## Alpha-Ink Hierarchy

The discipline is that every text tone is black at an opacity: 95% for display, 90% for body, 75% for logo marks and 54% for captions, with #615d59 as the single warm opaque exception for proof stats. Because the tones are translucent, they pick up the warmth of #f9f9f8 automatically when text sits on a Linen panel. A conventional fixed gray ramp cannot do that. The system breaks the moment someone hardcodes an opaque cool gray, or tints a heading blue for emphasis, because hierarchy then comes from hue instead of density. To extend it, add new steps only as alpha black, for example 40% for disabled text, and test them on both surfaces. If a new tone cannot be expressed as black thinned by opacity, it does not belong in the text ramp.

## Rationed Blue

The chromatic budget is one hue in three strengths: #0075de as fill, #005bab as ink and #e6f3fe as tint, and all three serve action. Everything else saturated is quarantined inside illustrations, sticker icons, mockup data and duotone portraits, where it reads as content rather than interface. Most SaaS pages spread their brand color across headings, icons and section backgrounds; here the blue appears on fewer than ten elements. The system breaks when a decorative hue such as #f64932 (decorative) migrates onto a badge or button, or when Lapis Mist becomes a section wash. To extend it, give every new interactive element the existing blue steps, and push any new color into imagery behind a frame so the button stays the only colored decision on screen.

## Tracking Discipline

Display type earns its density through negative letter spacing that scales faster than size. It runs -0.125px at 20px, -1.5px at 42px, -1.875px at 54px and -4.6px at 96px, nearly 0.05em at the top, against a conventional ceiling of about 0.02em. Paired with weight 600 or 700 and line-heights near 1.04, headlines become compact ink blocks that echo a document title rather than a billboard. The discipline breaks if a substitute font is dropped in without retuning the tracking, if line-height relaxes to the conventional 1.2, or if weight climbs to 800. To extend it, interpolate tracking for any new size, for example about -2.8px at 64px, and keep body sizes at 0px so the contrast between slab headlines and open text survives.

## Similar Brands

- **Coda** — The same doc-workspace pitch built from real product screenshots on a white canvas with one filled CTA color, though Coda spends more saturated color on section backgrounds.
- **Craft** — A shared document-as-hero composition with soft 12px framed mockups and low-alpha shadows, though Craft leans on gradients that Notion avoids entirely.
- **Linear** — The same aggressively negative-tracked Inter-family display headlines carrying hierarchy, inverted onto a near-black canvas.
- **Airtable** — Product UI as the hero image, a single blue primary button and a monotone customer logo strip, with heavier, more conventional card shadows.
- **Dropbox** — Hand-drawn illustration paired with a grotesk and one blue action color, though Dropbox pushes illustration hues into full-bleed brand surfaces.
